name: dingluo1205/AirbnbDataPipeline
what_it_holds: End-to-end pipeline (Airflow, S3, Spark/EMR, Redshift/Athena) that pulls Inside Airbnb review and listing CSVs, partitioning outputs by month and city in S3. No data committed to the repo itself; infrastructure/orchestration code only.
why_useful: A reusable, more production-grade version of the 'pull Inside Airbnb into cloud storage on a schedule' pattern; could be adapted to build our own point-in-time vintage store of Inside Airbnb dumps going forward, but does not itself unlock any historical (pre-2023) data.
time_coverage: current live Inside Airbnb archive only
themes: Inside Airbnb historical dump mirrors and archives (pre-2023 listings/calendar/reviews CSVs committed or released; archive.org mirrors referenced from GitHub)
Inside Airbnb New York City snapshots around Local Law 18 (2023-06 to 2024-03) stored in repos
why_all: A reusable, more production-grade version of the 'pull Inside Airbnb into cloud storage on a schedule' pattern; could be adapted to build our own point-in-time vintage store of Inside Airbnb dumps going forward, but does not itself unlock any historical (pre-2023) data.
Another reusable pipeline pattern specifically naming New York among its target cities; low value on its own since it holds no data and depends on Inside Airbnb's live (non-archival) CDN.

name: airbert-vln/bnb-dataset
what_it_holds: Scripts + two committed TSV files (airbnb-train-indoor-filtered.tsv, airbnb-test-indoor-filtered.tsv) of Airbnb listing photo-caption pairs (listing ID, photo ID, image URL, caption) scraped from Airbnb.com as of a 'Christmas 2019' snapshot, filtered to indoor images only, used to pretrain a vision-and-language-navigation model (the 'Airbert' CVPR 2021 paper by Guillaume Bono et al., not one of the named target authors but the closest thing to a large committed Airbnb scrape found on GitHub). Pipeline continues to LMDB visual features and JSON path-instruction pairs for robot navigation training, not economics.
why_useful: Marginal for KPI forecasting -- it is an image/caption dataset for ML vision research, not pricing/occupancy/nights data. Listed for completeness since it is a real, non-trivial airbnb.com-derived academic dataset with committed files, but it doesn't bear on any numbered gap directly.
geography: cities drawn from Wikipedia place listings, global, unspecified count
size_hint: pre-computed TSVs committed; scale not stated in README
duplicate_of_holding: No overlap with anything we hold; distinct modality (images/captions, not price/occupancy).
themes: Kaggle-style Airbnb listing snapshot datasets committed to GitHub (any city, any year), especially multi-year or multi-city collections
Airbnb reviews text corpora and review-date datasets on GitHub (review counts over time as a stays proxy)

why_all: Marginal for KPI forecasting -- it is an image/caption dataset for ML vision research, not pricing/occupancy/nights data. Listed for completeness since it is a real, non-trivial airbnb.com-derived academic dataset with committed files, but it doesn't bear on any numbered gap directly.

Not directly useful for KPI forecasting (image/caption data, not price or nights) but documents a working, non-trivial Airbnb-listing scraper built for an academic paper (used for indoor-scene research) — low relevance to ABNB thesis, flagged mainly to rule out as a source.

A ready-made, dozens-of-cities global Airbnb scraper/downloader (listings + reviews + captions) built and tested by an academic NLP/vision group, usable as a method reference for what fields are obtainable and how, though it scrapes airbnb.com directly (ToS question per repo rule 6) and ships no data itself.

Large-scale (listing-level) captioned photo dataset from real Airbnb listings worldwide at a single point in time (Dec 2019) -- could in principle be repurposed as a cross-market listing snapshot/description corpus (amenity mix, room-type text) predating most of what the team holds, though it is aimed at computer vision, not KPIs, and the authors note images are no longer guaranteed available. Also a working example of a non-airbnb-owned method for turning Airbnb.com into a TSV/image corpus -- flag as method only, not to be run (touches airbnb.com directly, a ToS decision per repo rules).

name: msr-ds3/airbnb
what_it_holds: Academic (Data Science Summer School / MSR-DS3) project titled 'Airbnb: Predicting Loyalty' with a committed raw_data folder, load_historical_data.R, and exploration/historical_exploration scripts (e.g. lou_listings_history_amenities.R, suggesting a Louisville, KY panel) analyzing host/guest return behavior over time using Inside Airbnb history; 280 commits.
why_useful: Possible longitudinal (multi-snapshot-over-time) Inside Airbnb panel for a city (Louisville) outside our current 13-city set, with host/guest repeat-booking features that could proxy loyalty/retention dynamics; needs a directory listing to confirm exact vintages/row counts before treating as more than a lead.
geography: Louisville, KY (inferred from file naming) plus possibly other cities
last_activity: unknown (280 commits, academic project, likely dated ~2018-2019 DS3 cohort)
duplicate_of_holding: Possibly a new city (Louisville) not in our panel; unconfirmed overlap otherwise.

why_all: Possible longitudinal (multi-snapshot-over-time) Inside Airbnb panel for a city (Louisville) outside our current 13-city set, with host/guest repeat-booking features that could proxy loyalty/retention dynamics; needs a directory listing to confirm exact vintages/row counts before treating as more than a lead.
